explanation: Electric potential V is the potential energy per unit charge at a point — how many joules each coulomb would carry there, measured in volts. Around a point charge V = k Q / r, which falls off like 1/r (more gently than the field's 1/r^2). Slide Q and the test distance r and read V off the curve in kilovolts; the work to carry a charge q between two points is just W = q*(V2 - V1), so it depends only on the potential difference, not the path.
bullets: V = k Q / r is energy per unit charge (volts = J/C).
Potential falls off as 1/r — slower than the 1/r^2 field.
Work to move charge q: W = q*ΔV, depends only on the voltage difference.
